comments.value:
U# is a third-party compiler plugin for unity and is not maintained by VRChat team. VRChat only officially supports the UdonGraph and the UdonAssembly langauge. U# simply compiles C# like code down into the official UdonAssembly, similar to how the graph compiles into UdonAssembly as well.
In my experience, most of the issues with Udon Graph are related directly to the graph GUI itself, rather than the raw uasm.
I will remind people that Udon is still considered alpha (as this canny name implies), so there is still much work to be done on it. Do keep in mind that the VRChat team is rather small all things considered. Patience is key.

We're constantly working on both the Udon VM and the Udon Graph to find and fix issues, as well as add new features. U# is awesome and all of its development comes from the community, not the VRChat team.

details:
I know this sounds dumb but please hear me out. The creation of Udon#, while absolutely incredible for programmers, has severely stinted development into the Udon graph system.
The issue is that the vast majority of people using Udon are only using U#, so a lot of the feedback and bug reports are coming from U# users. This has lead to huge flaws in the Udon graph system getting barely any attention and falling to the wayside.
As an example, Udon graphs had a bug where for no apparent reason, the graph would fail to compile. There would be no error and no way to tell it was broken until you tested it. Once you knew it was a broken, the only way to fix it was to duplicate it and delete the old one. This wasn't rare either, it happened almost every single time. This lead to many situations where you were left wondering if you made a mistake in the graph, or if it was just broken for no reason. This bug alone was directly responsible for everyone moving to U# development instead because it was so debilitating. It was reported on the canny early on but wasn't actually fixed until about 10 months later. This, in my opinion, is absolutely ridiculous. There is no way a bug that bad should have been left alive for so long. Anybody that used Udon graphs for more than 20 minutes should have run into this issue, so why wasn't it fixed earlier?
Udon# didn't have this issue, it was exclusive to graphs. I can only assume that the majority of the development team working on Udon was also using U# and didn't even know the bug existed.
The crux of the issue is that if development continues to be focused on Udon# instead of graphs, a lot of people new to world creation are going to be turned off about using Udon if basically everything is designed around U#. A lot of new creators don't have any programming experience and aren't going to learn an entire programming language just to make their own home world. The community stands to lose a lot of potential talent if graphs simply aren't being developed, tested, and bug fixed.
In essence, I'd just like more focus to put on graphs instead of U# getting all the attention. If graphs aren't maintained properly then the barrier of entry into world creation becomes monumental for newbies and will only encourage more content to be created on SDK2. Please remember that the only reason you don't see a lot of Udon graph issues on the canny is because people either get fed up and move to U# or just completely give up on trying to make it work. Making graphs more user and beginner friendly is absolutely essential if you want the community to move away from SDK2.
title: Put more focus on Udon graph development
